restoreTest.help: A backup only counts if it comes back. Each week, after that day's scheduled backup, restic checks the repository and reads back part of the stored data, then every website's newest restore point is read as a restore would read it: each database dump in full, which must end like a finished dump, and a spread of the home's files, which must match their recorded size. Nothing is written to the websites.

docs.title: Developer guide
docs.subtitle: How extensions work, the manifest format, webhooks and the admin page

overview.intro: An extension adds a feature to dPanel from outside: an uptime report, a billing bridge, a custom dashboard. It runs on its own server or host name, and can only use the parts of the dPanel API that you approve when installing it.
overview.how1: The extension's code never runs inside the panel. No PHP, Vue or shell code from an extension is loaded, and nothing runs as root.
overview.how2: On install the panel creates a service account for the extension with one API token, carrying exactly the scopes you tick. That account cannot sign in.
overview.how3: The extension calls the REST API with that token like any other API client. Every change it makes is in the activity log.
overview.how4: The panel can send the extension signed webhook events, such as a new or deleted website.
overview.how5: The extension can have one admin page, shown here in a sandboxed frame loaded from its own address.
overview.install1: Paste the extension's manifest below (or choose the file) and press Check manifest. Problems are listed by field.
overview.install2: Read what it asks for and tick only the scopes you agree to. It can never get a scope its manifest does not ask for, nor one you do not have.
overview.install3: Press Install. The API token and webhook secret are shown once: give both to the extension, usually in its own settings or environment.
overview.install4: To update, check the new version's manifest the same way. The token stays; its scopes become the ones you tick now.
overview.apiText: The extension sends its token as a Bearer header to this panel's API:

disable.label: Disable
disable.text: the token stops working, no events are sent and the page closes. Nothing is deleted; Enable turns it back on.

ping.label: Send test event
ping.text: sends a signed ping now and shows the answer.

rotate.label: New token and secret
rotate.text: makes new credentials, shown once. The old token stops working at once.

update.label: Update
update.text: install a newer manifest with the same id; new scopes are marked.

uninstall.label: Uninstall
uninstall.text: deletes the extension, its token and its service account. What it created through the API stays.

manifest.intro: The manifest is a JSON file (usually dpanel-extension.json) that describes the extension. Copy this example as a starting point:

keys.id: 3-64 lowercase letters, digits, dots and dashes, such as acme.uptime. The same for every version.
keys.name: Shown name, up to 80 characters.
keys.description: Shown to the admin, up to 500 characters. author works the same way.
keys.panel: dPanel versions it works with: space-separated comparators that must all hold, such as >=1.0 <2.0.
keys.scopes: API scopes it asks for: websites, dns, databases, mail, each :read or :write.
keys.ui_admin_page: title (up to 40 characters) and url of its admin page.
keys.webhook_url: Where events are sent. Required when events is set.
keys.events: Events it wants. Each needs the read (or write) scope of its area.

manifest.urls: Every address must use https:// (plain http:// only on 127.0.0.1 or localhost) and must not be on the panel's own host name. Serve the extension from another host name, such as uptime.example.com for a panel on panel.example.com.
manifest.strict: Unknown keys are refused, so a manifest written for a later format is never half read.

webhooks.intro: Events are sent as a signed POST with a JSON body to webhook.url. Version 1 sends:
webhooks.pingOnly: none; sent only from Send test event

headers.X_Dpanel_Delivery: The event id, the same on every retry. Use it to skip duplicates.
headers.X_Dpanel_Signature: sha256= followed by the hex HMAC-SHA256 of timestamp.body, keyed with the webhook secret.

webhooks.verifyText: Check the signature and that the timestamp is within 5 minutes before trusting anything in the body:
webhooks.retry: Answer with any 2xx status within 10 seconds. Anything else is a failure: the panel tries up to three times (after 10 and 60 seconds) and shows the last error on the extension's card. Redirects are not followed. Events are queued, so the panel's queue worker must be running.

page.intro: If the manifest has ui.admin_page, an Open button shows that page inside the panel.
page.point1: It is loaded in a sandboxed frame (scripts, forms and popups only) with no referrer. It runs in an opaque origin: it cannot read the panel's cookies, storage or page, and cannot use its own cookies either.
page.point2: The panel page only allows frames from your extension's origin.
page.point3: Render the page on your server and carry state in your own links or forms, since the page has no cookies.
page.frameTitle: Allow the panel to frame you
page.frameText: Your page must send a header that lets this panel embed it:
page.contextText: The panel adds dpanel_context to your page's URL. It names the viewer (id, name, role), the locale and an expiry 5 minutes ahead, signed with the webhook secret. Check it on your server before showing anything:

limits.item1: dPanel does not run extension code. Host the extension yourself; running it on this server is planned.
limits.item2: One UI slot (the admin page) and two events (website.created, website.deleted).
limits.item3: No marketplace or signed packages: you decide whom to trust by reading the manifest.
limits.item4: Extensions are for admins only; resellers and users cannot install them.
limits.more: The full reference is docs/extensions.md in the dPanel repository.

runtime.fromDocker: Leaving Docker removes this site's container. Files in the site folder stay.

queue.removeConfirm: Remove the "{queue}" worker and stop its processes?
queue.title: Queue Workers
queue.help: Runs {cmd} as background services. They start automatically when the server boots and restart if they crash.
queue.restartHint: Re-apply every worker and restart it, e.g. after deploying new code
queue.connectionHelp: e.g. {a} or {b}. Leave blank to use the app's default.
queue.timeoutHelp: Keep the timeout a few seconds below the connection's {key} in {file} (90 by default), or a slow job can run twice.
queue.empty: No queue workers yet. Add one to process jobs dispatched by this app.
queue.summary: {processes} process · {tries} tries · {timeout}s timeout · {memory} MB · sleep {sleep}s | {processes} processes · {tries} tries · {timeout}s timeout · {memory} MB · sleep {sleep}s

docker.runImageHelp: The panel runs one container for this site.
docker.usePort: Use a running stack or port
docker.usePortHelp: WordPress + MySQL, Kibana, any compose app.
docker.noStack: None: just a port on this server
docker.stackHelp: With a stack, this site's Start, Stop, Restart and Logs act on it. Create stacks under Docker → Stacks.
docker.targetPort: Server port to send the domain to
docker.targetPortHelp: The port the app publishes on the server, e.g. {example} in a compose file means 8085. SSL, IP rules and redirects of this site keep working.
docker.anyImage: Or enter any image below. Its Docker Hub page lists the port it listens on and the folder it reads.
docker.imageHelp: Pulled from Docker Hub when it is not on the server yet, e.g. {a} or {b}.
docker.containerPortHelp: The port inside the container (often 80, 3000 or 8080). dPanel picks the server-side port and sends this domain to it.
docker.mountHelp: The site's root folder {path} appears at this path in the container. Upload and edit its files with this website's File Manager, then restart the container. Leave blank to mount nothing.
docker.envHelp: Passwords and settings the image asks for. Values are stored encrypted.
docker.public: Also open its port to the internet
docker.publicHelp: Off: reachable only through this domain. On: also at http://server-ip:port. Docker opens the port itself, so the server firewall does not block it.

dockerService.stopStackConfirm: Stop stack {stack}? The site shows an error page until it starts again.
dockerService.stopConfirm: Stop the container? The site shows an error page until it starts again.
dockerService.redeployConfirm: Deploy stack {stack} again from its compose file?
dockerService.recreateConfirm: Recreate the container with the current settings? Files in the site folder stay; anything else inside the container is lost.
dockerService.publicConfirm: Open port {port} to the internet? Anyone can then reach the app at {url}, and the server firewall does not block it.
dockerService.title: Docker Service
dockerService.notInstalled: Docker is no longer installed on this server, so this container cannot run. Install it with {cmd}.
dockerService.stackFailed: The last action on the stack failed. Open Logs, or open the stack to see which service is down.
dockerService.containerFailed: The container could not start. Open Logs, or check the image name and port in Runtime settings, then press Recreate.
dockerService.domainSent: The domain is sent to 127.0.0.1:{port}. If it shows an error page, check that the app is running and publishes that port.
dockerService.openStack: Open the stack: services, logs, compose file
dockerService.noStack: No stack is linked, so start and stop the app where it runs. Pick its stack in Runtime settings to control it from here.
dockerService.openPortHelp: Off: only through the domain above. On: also by IP. The container is recreated to apply it.
dockerService.editFiles: Upload and edit in File Manager
dockerService.restartAfter: Restart the container after changing config files.
dockerService.noMount: No folder is mounted, so the app only has what is inside its image. Set "Site folder inside the container" in Runtime settings to edit files from the File Manager.
dockerService.step1: Upload your files to the site folder with the File Manager (zips can be extracted there).
dockerService.step2: Press Restart so the app picks up changed config files. Use Recreate after a new image tag or changed settings.
dockerService.step3: If the site shows an error page, open Logs: a missing variable or a wrong port is the usual cause.

edgeCache.title: Edge Cache
edgeCache.subtitle: Page caching for {domain}, served by this server.
edgeCache.system: This is the panel's own website. It is never cached, so every page always shows live data.
edgeCache.purgeHelp: Remove cached copies after you change content, so the next visit fetches it fresh.
edgeCache.urlsHelp: One URL or path per line. A URL without ?query also clears its query-string variants.
edgeCache.prefixesHelp: Every cached page whose path starts with one of these is removed.
edgeCache.offText: Every request goes to your server.
edgeCache.standardText: Caches static files and anything your app marks cacheable with Cache-Control.
edgeCache.cacheAllText: Also caches HTML pages. Pages that set cookies, logged-in visitors and bypass paths are still skipped.
edgeCache.cachingHelp: Copies of your pages are kept in the server's memory and sent without running your app.
edgeCache.edgeTtlHelp: How long a copy is kept when your app does not say (s-maxage wins when it does).
edgeCache.browserTtlHelp: How long visitors' browsers keep cached responses. A purge cannot reach browsers.
edgeCache.bypassPathsHelp: One path prefix per line, e.g. /wp-admin.
edgeCache.bypassCookies: Skip the cache for visitors with these cookies
edgeCache.bypassCookiesHelp: Cookie name prefixes, one per line, e.g. wordpress_logged_in_.
edgeCache.serveStale: Keep the site up when the app fails
edgeCache.serveStaleHelp: If your app returns a 5xx error, visitors get the last cached copy (kept up to a day).
edgeCache.ignoreQueryHelp: /page?utm_source=x and /page share one copy. Leave off if your pages change with ?parameters.
edgeCache.activityHelp: Counted since the edge gateway last started.
edgeCache.checkHelp: Check a page with {cmd}: HIT and STALE came from the cache, MISS and EXPIRED were fetched and stored, DYNAMIC was not cacheable, BYPASS matched a bypass rule.
edgeCache.devHelp: Skip the cache for 3 hours while you edit the site. It turns itself off.

panelLink.title: Live connection to another dPanel
panelLink.intro: Link another dPanel with an API token made there. Then take websites or the whole panel from it, or send them to it, without downloading or uploading a backup. Run a sync later to move only the files that changed.
panelLink.noConnection: Add a connection to see the other panel's websites.
panelLink.step1: On the other panel open Profile menu → API Tokens.
panelLink.step2: Make a token with the Live migration scope: Read to take from it, Write to also send to it.
panelLink.step3: Enter that panel's address and the token here.
panelLink.token: API token from the other panel
panelLink.name: Name
panelLink.thisPanelUrl: This panel's address, for linking from the other side:
panelLink.makeTokenHere: Make a token on this panel
panelLink.removeConfirm: Remove the connection to {name}? Delete its token on the other panel too.
panelLink.noPullScope: This connection's token can't take from the other panel. Make a token with Live migration: Read there.
panelLink.noPushScope: This connection's token can't send to the other panel. Make a token with Live migration: Write there.
panelLink.ownerAuto: Same email as on the other panel, else me
panelLink.manageDns: Create a DNS zone here for new websites
panelLink.deleteMissing: Sync: also remove files here that the other panel no longer has
panelLink.manageDnsThere: Create a DNS zone on the other panel for new websites
panelLink.deleteMissingThere: Sync: also remove files there that this panel no longer has
panelLink.copyHelp: Copy: files and database; a missing website is created here, an existing one's files and database go to its .trash first. Sync: only files that differ (.gitignore applies); the database is not touched.
panelLink.copyThereHelp: Copy: files and database; a missing website is created on the other panel, an existing one's files and database go to its .trash first. Sync: only files that differ (.gitignore applies); the database is not touched.
panelLink.wholePullHelp: The other panel makes a full backup and this panel downloads it. It then appears below in the backup list: restoring it replaces this panel's .env, data and panel database.
panelLink.wholePushHelp: This panel makes a full backup and sends it. Restore it on the other panel under Migrate → DPanel to DPanel: that replaces its .env, data and panel database.

delete.title: Delete {name}?
delete.help: Removes the database from the panel.
delete.dropTitle: Also drop it from the server
delete.dropHelp: The database and its user are dropped, and the data is gone for good. Unticked, the database stays on the server.
